name: Counterpoint
idea: A shared bar connects J and T into one compact signature.
risk: The most restrained direction; less expressive than the script.

name: Imprint
idea: Contrasting serif lettering gives JT an independent record-label character.
risk: Fine serif details need a simplified cut for tiny icons.

name: Cutline
idea: A drawn, chamfered alphabet creates a bold nameplate for the catalog.
risk: The hardest-edged option may feel less intimate for R&B.

name: Signed
idea: Flowing lettering and one original sweep put the producer behind the name.
risk: The full signature needs more width at small sizes.

name: Pocket
idea: A rounded j/t pairing gives the store a warm, approachable rhythm.
risk: Its softer character is less severe than the industrial option.
